summary: Operator UX is mixed. The promotion workflows, gate validators, and `oya submit` shell are pleasant: sane defaults, idempotent, helpful echoes, clear error prefixes. The new `oya-vcs-changeset-state-app append` CLI is the soft spot — the happy path requires the operator to memorize ~5 things (`cs_<RFC3339-Z>_<8-hex>` ID grammar, the closed 13-value enum spelling, k=v evidence syntax, the from_state/to_state ordering, and the implicit default log path). There is no `--help`, no enum listing on parse failure, no ID-grammar validation, no `--list-states`, and no `oya vcs` umbrella for the operator-facing commands referenced by ADR-0110 (`oya vcs done/abandon`). New-contributor minutes-estimate: ~18-22 min for a clean first append, exceeding the F4 ≤15-min target for kernel-public-API change_class. Findings are MAJOR (not BLOCKER): the surface is functionally usable and well-documented in README/IP-001, but the discoverability gap and the silent default-budget stamping invite misuse.

findings.issue: USAGE string is the only discovery surface — no `--help`/`-h` flag, no `--list-states` enumeration, and no top-level subcommand listing. A new operator who runs the binary with no args sees only the one-line USAGE and must read the source or README to learn that `append` is the only subcommand and that `--to-state` accepts exactly 13 specific snake_case strings. The trigger-question 'does this require memorizing more than 3 things' fails: changeset-id grammar + closed enum + evidence k=v + log path + emitter convention = 5+.
findings.remediation: Add `--help`/`-h` that prints USAGE plus a `Subcommands:` section and `Valid --to-state values:` list (cheap: iterate `ChangesetState::ALL.map(as_wire)`). Same fix on `oya gate validate changeset-state-{monotonicity,enum-closed}`.

findings.issue: When `--to-state` is misspelled the error is `--to-state value `pr_oepn` is not in the closed 13-value enum per ADR-0110` — it names the policy but never lists the 13 values. The operator has to grep the kernel for `as_wire` to find the canonical spellings. F4 trigger 'does the error message tell them exactly what to fix' fails — it tells them what's wrong but not what to type.
findings.remediation: Append `valid values: opened, working, verified, pr_open, ci_running, ci_passed, reviewed, merged_dev, staged, produced, abandoned, rejected, cost_exhausted` to both the to_state and from_state error branches. Generate via `ChangesetState::ALL.iter().map(|s| s.as_wire()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")` so the message stays in sync if the enum ever grows (even though it is closed today).

findings.issue: `build_candidate_event` silently stamps `STUB_USD=100.0`, `STUB_TOKENS=10_000_000`, `STUB_INVOCATIONS=100` and an `ed25519-stub:` signature on every append, with no flag to override and no warning printed to the operator on stdout/stderr. An agent calling this in production will produce event-log rows that pass the validator but lie about cost-budget remaining, and the only signal is the `ed25519-stub:` substring buried in the JSON. Per F4 'silent-mismatch-instead-of-error' anti-pattern.
findings.remediation: Print a single-line `WARN: stub budget + stub signature stamped (wave-A; wave-B will replace)` on stderr at the top of every append. When wave-B lands, gate the warning on `OYA_VCS_ALLOW_STUB_SIGNATURE=1` so production agents must opt in explicitly.

findings.issue: The `--changeset` value is accepted as any free-form string, but the README at `registry/vcs/README.md:38` and kernel doc at `lib.rs:166` declare a strict `cs_<RFC3339-Z>_<8-hex>` grammar. A typo like `cs-2026-05-16T...` (dash instead of underscore) sails past parsing, lands in the log, and only surfaces later when downstream tooling that does parse the grammar trips. Trigger 'failure mode when someone makes a typo or partial fill' fails — failure mode is silent acceptance now, hard-to-debug crash later.
findings.remediation: Add a `validate_changeset_id_grammar(&str) -> Result<(), String>` helper to the kernel and call it at parse time in both the app's `parse_append_args` and the gate's `parse_event`. Error message: `--changeset "cs-bad" does not match cs_<RFC3339-Z>_<8-hex>; example: cs_2026-05-16T01:00:00Z_a1b2c3d4`.

findings.issue: The argv parser is positional-strict (`while let Some(flag) ... iter.next()`) so a partial fill where the operator types `--evidence` without a value steals the *next* flag's name as its value: `append --changeset cs1 --to-state opened --evidence --emitted-by foo` parses `evidence="--emitted-by"` and then fails at `flag `foo` requires a value`. The error is unhelpful (it accuses `foo` of being a flag). F4 'failure mode of partial fill' fails.
findings.remediation: Reject any `value` that starts with `--` (with override `--evidence=` long-form supported), or refactor to `clap` derive — the manual parser has now grown three call sites with the same shape and is the wrong abstraction at this point. Same fix needed in `submit.rs::parse_submit_args` (`--title --body ""` exhibits the same bug).

findings.issue: The 'Trigger downstream production promotion (PAT-only)' step is silently skipped when `WORKFLOW_PAT` is unset (`if: success() && env.WORKFLOW_PAT != ''`). An operator who deploys this repo without configuring `WORKFLOW_PAT` sees a green workflow run but production lags up to 1 hour behind dev (until the hourly cron fires). There is no log line in the *succeeding* workflow saying 'WORKFLOW_PAT not set; production will lag up to 1h via cron fallback'. Trigger 'common case fast, edge case explicit' fails — the cron-fallback edge case is invisible from a CI dashboard.
findings.remediation: Add a second always-run step `name: Report WORKFLOW_PAT status` that prints either `WORKFLOW_PAT configured — downstream triggered` or `WORKFLOW_PAT MISSING — production will lag up to 1h until hourly cron fires (configure repo secret to fix)`. Same pattern wanted on `promote-staging-to-production.yml` whenever it grows a downstream trigger.

findings.issue: ADR-0110 documents operator-facing commands `oya vcs abandon --changeset <id>` and `oya vcs done --changeset <id> --subscribe <callback-url>` but PR #5 ships ONLY the lower-level `oya-vcs-changeset-state-app append`. An operator reading the ADR will type `oya vcs abandon ...`, get `unknown command`, and have no obvious next step. Trigger 'how many minutes does a new contributor need to add/use this correctly' suffers — they will hunt for ~10min before finding the long-form binary name. Implicit-conventions-not-declared anti-pattern.
findings.remediation: Either (a) add a stub `oya vcs {abandon,done}` subcommand to `oya-dev-cli` that shells through to the app with the right `--to-state`, or (b) add a 'Operator entry point (wave-A)' note at the top of ADR-0110 explicitly stating: 'Until wave-B lands the `oya vcs` umbrella, run `cargo run -q -p oya-vcs-changeset-state-app -- append --changeset <id> --to-state abandoned`.' Option (a) is preferable — README already documents the long form and operators copy-pasted it once already (`registry/vcs/README.md:36`).

findings.issue: Default `--log` is `registry/vcs/changeset-event-log.json`, a *relative* path. Running the binary from anywhere except the repo root either reads/writes a fresh empty log in the cwd (creating an inconsistent second log file) or fails with a confusing 'mkdir -p registry/vcs: …'. Trigger 'common case fast' partly fails for operators running from a worktree subdirectory.
findings.remediation: Resolve the default to the workspace root (e.g., walk up looking for a `Cargo.toml` with `[workspace]`) OR, simpler, fail-explicit when cwd is not the workspace root: `oya-vcs-changeset-state-app: refusing to use default --log from cwd=<cwd>; pass --log <abs-path> or run from workspace root`.

findings.issue: `dedup_key = <changeset_id>_<to_state>_<at>` uses second-precision RFC3339, so two appends in the same second for the same changeset+to_state collide and the second one is rejected as `DuplicateDedupKey`. The error tells the operator the dedup_key but not the remediation. Edge case: an agent retrying within the same second (common for a fast loop).
findings.remediation: Either bump precision to milliseconds in `format_rfc3339_utc`, OR catch `DuplicateDedupKey` in `run()` and rewrite the message to `same changeset+state appended within 1s; either re-emit dedup_key=<x> deliberately (no-op) or wait 1s before retrying`.

findings.issue: `--evidence k=v,k=v` overloads the comma — operators cannot put a comma inside a value (e.g., `head_sha=abc,reviewers=alice,bob` will be parsed as 3 pairs and fail on `bob`). No escape syntax documented. Trigger 'failure mode when someone makes a typo or partial fill' fails for any value containing a comma.
findings.remediation: Document the no-commas-in-values restriction in USAGE, AND/OR support repeated `--evidence k=v` flags (idiomatic and unambiguous). Repeated-flag form is a 5-line change: `"--evidence" => evidence_pairs.push(value)`.

findings.issue: Comment says: 'ADR-0110 §"The 9 states", actually 10 numbered 0..=9; the ADR prose "9 advancing" miscount is resolved here by counting the table rows literally'. Operators reading the kernel and the ADR get conflicting counts ('9 advancing' vs 10) — a small but real cognitive-load source for the next contributor.
findings.remediation: Fix the ADR prose to say `10 advancing states` so kernel and ADR agree, OR add an `#### Errata` block under ADR-0110 §The 9 states pointing at the kernel comment. Cheap; eliminates a stumble.

findings.issue: `is_terminal()` returns true for `Produced` (an advancing terminal) AND for `Abandoned/Rejected/CostExhausted` (terminal-fail), conflating two operator-relevant categories. The doc-comment says 'three terminal-fail states' but the impl returns true for four states. A future caller writing `if state.is_terminal() { mark_failed() }` will silently mark `Produced` as a failure.
findings.remediation: Either rename to `is_terminal_state()` and add a sibling `is_terminal_fail()` that excludes `Produced`, or split into `is_terminal_success()` / `is_terminal_fail()` / `is_terminal()`. The kernel docstring already calls out 'three terminal-fail states' so the asymmetry is undocumented surface today.

findings.issue: Both gate validators silently treat a missing-or-empty log as PASS (lines 57-62 and 63-68). An operator who deletes the file by accident, or whose CI runs in a worktree with the wrong cwd, will see `0 events checked` and a green gate. Trigger 'silent-mismatch-instead-of-error' fails — empty success looks identical to passing success.
findings.remediation: Print `note: log not present at <path> — treating as vacuously valid` on stderr when the early-return fires. Optionally add `--require-non-empty` flag for CI runs that want to enforce the file exists.

findings.issue: `HARNESS_SIDECAR_PREFIXES = [".omc/", ".omx/", ".grit/", "target/"]` is a hard-coded constant. If a new agent harness lands a `.vox/` or `.icm/` sidecar, every `oya submit` will refuse to push with a generic 'working tree has uncommitted changes' message — no hint that the cause was a hook-written sidecar.
findings.remediation: Either (a) load prefixes from `registry/vcs/agent-sidecar-prefixes.yaml` or (b) when the dirty entries are *all* under known dotdirs (`.something/`), print 'oya submit: detected agent-sidecar dirty entries (<paths>); add the prefix to HARNESS_SIDECAR_PREFIXES if benign' to give the operator a finger to pull on.

findings.issue: Cron schedules `*/30 * * * *` and `17 * * * *` lack inline operator-facing comments explaining 'why these specific cadences'. The header comments mention them but the cron line itself is bare. A future operator tweaking cadence has no in-line reminder of the canary-window-15min/full-cohort-1h reasoning.
findings.remediation: Add a same-line comment, e.g., `- cron: '*/30 * * * *'  # 30min — half the eventual 15min canary window, leaves headroom`.

findings.issue: The README example uses `cs_<ulid>` as a placeholder, but the kernel docstring (`lib.rs:166`) and the dedup-key construction expect `cs_<RFC3339-Z>_<8-hex>`. ULID and RFC3339+hex are *not* the same encoding. A copy-paste-and-edit operator will produce a malformed ID. Trigger 'implicit-conventions-not-declared'.
findings.remediation: Replace `cs_<ulid>` with the canonical example `cs_2026-05-16T01:00:00Z_a1b2c3d4` in the README code block, and add one line: 'Format: `cs_<RFC3339-Z>_<8-hex-rand>` per ADR-0110 §Identifier shape.'
